nodes.title: Prompt v15 — fundo trocado em TODOS os frames
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
Woman: the woman from Video 1, reproduced exactly as she appears there: her identity, face, skin tone, bare shoulders and upper chest, her poses, gestures, hand movements, facial expressions and lip movements. Her hair is dark brown-black and curly. Most of it is gathered in a high bun, and a long, thick lock of her own hair hangs down in front of her into the bath. Throughout the video she holds this lock of hair in her hands, lifting and stretching it, exactly as in Video 1. The lock always looks like real human hair, with the same color and texture as the rest of her hair: dark, wet, glossy, curly strands. Her skin looks exactly as in Video 1, smooth, bare and clean. The only parts of her ever visible are her head, shoulders, upper chest, arms, hands and the lock of hair, exactly the same parts visible in Video 1. Everything else of her is hidden inside the bath.

summary:
Video 1 itself, with a single change: over the full 5-second duration, the bath water progressively transforms from the original water visible in the first frame into a dense, heavy, highly viscous dark green mass with the color and richly textured surface of Picture 1, like thick wet clay, dense mud or heavy molasses, closer to a soft paste than to a liquid. The transformation must happen naturally from bottom to top, as if a dark green dirty ink-like contamination is blooming upward through the water from the bottom of the tub. It should feel like a cloud of grime, algae, pigment and sludge rising through the water volume, gradually spreading upward until the whole bath becomes green, murky and mossy. The green material must not appear as a layer painted on top of the water, and the transformation must not look like a crossfade or sudden texture replacement. Everything else is identical to Video 1, frame by frame: the woman and her performance, the timing, the bathroom, the lighting, the framing, the field of view and the 16:9 aspect ratio.

retention_analysis:
Video 1 is retained as the base footage for everything outside the bath contents: the woman’s identity, appearance, hair and clean skin; her poses, gestures, hand movements, expressions and lip movements, including the way she handles and stretches her lock of hair; exactly which parts of her body are visible above the surface; the fill level; the bathroom with all its objects; the lighting and color; the camera view, framing, field of view, 16:9 aspect ratio and timing of its single static shot. Picture 1 is retained for the final color, surface texture, tonal variation and contrast of the bath contents. The bath begins with the original water appearance of Video 1 and progressively transforms throughout the 5-second shot until the final frame reaches the appearance of Picture 1. The transformation grows upward from the bottom of the bath like submerged green-black ink and dirt clouds spreading through the water. Nothing else from Picture 1 is used: not its framing, crop, scale, lighting or subject.

detailed_description:
[Shot 1] 0-5s: The exact view of Video 1: a single static high-angle overhead shot looking straight down into a cream-colored acrylic bathtub. Every frame, starting with the very first one, has exactly the same framing, field of view, scale, 16:9 aspect ratio and composition as the matching frame of Video 1. The tub, the woman and every object occupy exactly the same place and size in the frame as in Video 1 for the whole video. The only motion in the frame comes from the woman and the changing material in the tub.

The woman sits at the head end of the tub, at the top of the frame, facing the camera, submerged to the chest, head tilted down toward her hands. Every movement of her arms and hands follows Video 1 exactly. She lifts the long lock of her own hair out of the bath, slowly pulls it apart with her fingers and stretches it between her hands. She lays it across the surface in front of her chest, lets it sink, then gathers it up and stretches it again.

The lock of hair stays dark brown-black for the whole video: wet, glossy, curly human hair, separating into thin dark strands as she pulls it apart. As the bath contents progressively become denser and more viscous, the changing material increasingly clings to the hair while submerged, then slowly releases it as she lifts it, sliding off in progressively thicker and heavier strings that sag back into the bath, leaving the hair its natural dark color.

The bath remains filled to the same level as the water in Video 1, up to her chest. The rest of the tub, from just below her chest down to the bottom edge of the frame and across to both side walls, remains the same open expanse occupied by the bath contents exactly as in Video 1. Nothing rises out of this area at any moment: it contains only the transforming bath material, with her hands and hair moving through it right in front of her chest. It remains one continuous, unbroken surface for the whole video.

At the first frame, the bath contents still look like the original water in Video 1. The transformation begins below the water, at the bottom of the tub, not on the surface. Dark green contamination starts to appear beneath the water as submerged cloudy blooms, like thick dirty ink dispersing upward through the water. These first contaminations look like underwater clouds of grime, algae-rich pigment, mud and sludge, rising slowly from the bottom toward the surface.

As the transformation progresses, these dark green clouds expand upward and outward through the water volume. The effect should feel like ink in water, but heavier, dirtier and denser: soft cloudy billows, spreading plumes, submerged marbling and blooming contamination rising from the lower part of the tub toward the upper layer. The original water remains visible at first above and around these clouds, so the change clearly reads as a bottom-to-top transformation.

The green coloration must remain highly non-uniform throughout the transition, with irregular dark olive-green areas, deep forest-green areas, near-black regions, brown-green contamination and brighter vivid green pigment zones developing at different densities inside the water. The transformation must never turn the whole bath into a flat, uniform green tint. It must always feel like layered dirty contamination physically spreading through the water, with visible cloudy structures and uneven saturation.

By the middle of the shot, the lower and central portions of the bath are already heavily transformed, while the upper portions and shallower areas still retain more of the original water appearance. The viewer should clearly feel that the contamination has risen from the bottom and is progressively taking over the water from below. The distinction between cleaner water and darker contaminated regions remains spatially irregular, organic and cloud-like.

Toward the final part of the shot, the rising clouds of contamination merge more and more, filling the full depth of the bath and reaching the surface completely. The bath contents become progressively darker, less transparent, more opaque and more viscous. The original water appearance slowly gives way to a dense, heavy material like thick wet clay, dense mud or heavy molasses. The surface develops the richly mottled, marbled and grainy appearance of Picture 1. Patches of brighter vivid green pigment become embedded within deeper forest-green and near-black areas, with tiny bright glints and specular flecks of warm light catching on the increasingly wet, uneven surface.

By the final frame, the transformation is complete. The bath is filled with a dense, heavy, highly viscous, opaque mass instead of water, like thick wet clay, dense mud or heavy molasses. It is closer to a soft paste than to a liquid: it barely flows, has real weight and body, and holds its shape for a moment before slowly sagging. Its final look follows Picture 1 closely. It has a deep dark green base, near-black in the shadowed areas, with a mottled, marbled, grainy surface. Patches of brighter, vivid green pigment glow just beneath and on the surface, especially near the bottom of the frame. Darker and lighter green zones blend into each other in irregular blotches, and tiny bright glints and specular flecks of warm light catch on the wet, uneven surface.

The physical behavior of the bath contents changes progressively together with the visual transformation. At the beginning, it still behaves like the original water of Video 1. As the green contamination spreads upward from below and concentration increases, the material becomes progressively slower, thicker and heavier. Water-like ripples and fluid movement gradually reduce. The surface increasingly resists displacement, becoming more sluggish and viscous.

Near the final state, the mass moves extremely slowly and heavily, nothing like water. It no longer ripples, sloshes, splashes or forms normal waves. Its surface stays almost still, with only slow, heavy deformations. Where her hands and hair push through it, it resists. It parts reluctantly, bulges up in thick, rounded mounds and deep folds that keep their shape for a moment, and leaves soft dents and trails that close up very slowly, carrying the mottled pattern and bright green patches with them. When she lifts her hands, the mass clings for an instant, stretches into short, thick, heavy strands, then lets go and sinks slowly back into the bath, leaving her skin bare and clean as in Video 1. All motion of the mass is slow, heavy and contained inside the bath.

The green transformation must always originate visually from below and inside the bath water. It must rise from the bottom toward the surface like a growing submerged cloud of ink, dirt and musky contamination. It must never behave like green paint, moss, sludge or a texture appearing on top of the original water surface. It must look like the water itself is gradually becoming contaminated from the bottom up, with the green material spreading through the depth of the water and gradually replacing the original liquid state.

The inner walls of the tub above the bath contents, the rim, the tiles and every object stay perfectly clean and unchanged, exactly as in Video 1, for the whole video. The bath contents meet the inner tub walls in a single clean line, with spotless walls above it. The bathroom, its objects and its lighting are exactly as in Video 1. No dialogue or narration.

TILES AUTO (SyncTile ≥ 6.4): tile_width/height = 0 nos Conditioning e Guider calculam os tiles pelo canvas. Troque o ResolutionSelector (16:9, 1:1, 9:16...) e os tiles se ajustam sozinhos (~1.3 MP/tile, menor nº de tiles).

1:1 (quadrado) — Estágio 1 ≈1024×1024 (1 tile); Estágio 2 3.7 MP ≈1920×1920 com tiles 1120×1120 = 2×2 (min_overlap 16, janelas 124/39). Resultado 1:1. Requer SyncTile ≥ 6.3.

v32 · vid2vid (v27 guide2) + receita Pika H3 Flex · bruxosdovfx
• Pika H3 Flex ref2va em 1.0 por um LoraLoaderModelOnly direto no modelo (como no workflow do Pika).
• Sampler lcm; estágio 1 sigmas do Pika 1.0 / 0.972973 / 0.923077 / 0.8 / 0.571429 / 0.333333 / 0; estágio 2 cauda 0.8 / 0.571429 / 0.333333 / 0.
• Janelas: blend windows (joint) + freenoise nos dois guiders (SyncTile ≥ 6.3).
• Velocidade: estágio 1 = 1 tile por janela (1 MP); estágio 2 = upscale 3.7 MP (~2592×1504) com tiles 1440×896 = 4 tiles por janela. Vertical: 896×1440. Sol-Attn em bypass.
• ATENÇÃO: as pilhas de LoRA do grupo Models estão com toggle OFF (Background Replace v3, character swap etc. NÃO são aplicados). Ligue o toggle se quiser usá-los.

[Shot 1] 0-17.7s: The exact view of Video 1: a single static high-angle overhead shot looking straight down into a cream-colored acrylic bathtub. Every frame, starting with the very first one, has exactly the same framing, field of view, scale, 16:9 aspect ratio and composition as the matching frame of Video 1. The tub, the woman and every object occupy exactly the same place and size in the frame as in Video 1 for the whole video. The only motion in the frame comes from the woman and the mass in the tub.

The woman sits at the head end of the tub, at the top of the frame, facing the camera, submerged to the chest, head tilted down toward her hands. Every movement of her arms and hands follows Video 1 exactly. She lifts the long lock of her own hair out of the bath, slowly pulls it apart with her fingers and stretches it between her hands. She lays it across the surface in front of her chest, lets it sink, then gathers it up and stretches it again.

The lock of hair stays dark brown-black for the whole video: wet, glossy, curly human hair, separating into thin dark strands as she pulls it apart. As she lifts it, the dense mass slowly releases it, sliding off in thick, heavy strings that sag back into the bath, leaving the hair its natural dark color.

The mass fills the tub high, up to her chest, at the same level as the water in Video 1. The rest of the tub, from just below her chest down to the bottom edge of the frame and across to both side walls, is an open expanse of its surface, exactly as the water area in Video 1. Nothing rises out of this area at any moment: it contains only the mass, with her hands and hair moving through it right in front of her chest. It stays one continuous, unbroken, textured surface for the whole video.

From the first frame to the last, the tub is filled with a dense, heavy, highly viscous, opaque mass instead of water, like thick wet clay, dense mud or heavy molasses. It is closer to a soft paste than to a liquid: it barely flows, has real weight and body, and holds its shape for a moment before slowly sagging. Its look follows Picture 1 closely and stays rich and varied in every frame. It is a deep dark green base, near-black in the shadowed areas, with a mottled, marbled, grainy surface. Patches of brighter, vivid green pigment glow just beneath and on the surface, especially near the bottom of the frame. Darker and lighter green zones blend into each other in irregular blotches, and tiny bright glints and specular flecks of warm light catch on the wet, uneven surface. Each zone keeps its tonal variation, grain, bright green patches, dark blotches and glints with the same density, sharpness and contrast in the last frame as in the first. Throughout the video the mass never becomes flatter, simpler, softer or more uniform in color.

The mass moves extremely slowly and heavily, nothing like water. It never ripples, sloshes, splashes or forms waves. Its surface stays almost still, with only slow, heavy deformations. Where her hands and hair push through it, it resists. It parts reluctantly, bulges up in thick, rounded mounds and deep folds that keep their shape for a moment, and leaves soft dents and trails that close up very slowly, carrying the mottled pattern and bright green patches with them. When she lifts her hands, the mass clings for an instant, stretches into short, thick, heavy strands, then lets go and sinks slowly back into the bath, leaving her skin bare and clean as in Video 1. All motion of the mass is slow, heavy and contained inside the bath.

The inner walls of the tub above the mass, the rim, the tiles and every object stay perfectly clean and unchanged, exactly as in Video 1, for the whole video. The mass meets the inner tub walls in a single clean, straight line, with spotless walls above it. The bathroom, its objects and its lighting are exactly as in Video 1. No dialogue or narration.
